The '''Mariposa-Rhovland maritime dispute''' was an Istragarde-era dispute between the [[People's Republic of Mariposa]] and [[Imperial Rhovland]] over the eastern [[Straits of Avangard]].

== Background ==

The [[Treaty of the Concord of Istragarde]] created broad maritime-rights language but left enforcement weak. In the eastern strait, Mariposa and Rhovland claimed overlapping economic rights, especially around fishing, oil exploration, patrol routes, and commercial traffic.

Rhovland treated the strait as a critical artery for naval and commercial fleets. Mariposa treated it as an essential economic zone that could support the post-revolutionary state's development.

== 1983 Standoff ==

In 1983, Mariposa sent survey ships escorted by naval corvettes to explore potential underwater oil reserves. Rhovland responded by dispatching destroyers, creating a weeks-long standoff.

The [[Istragarde Tribunal]] ruled in favor of shared exploitation rights, but neither side complied fully. Mariposa accused Rhovland of economic sabotage, while Rhovland condemned Mariposa for reckless maritime adventurism.

== Legacy By 1994 ==

The dispute remained unresolved by the 1994-back window. It showed how the Istragarde framework could define procedures for maritime claims without forcing powerful states or determined revolutionary governments to obey the outcome.
